blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Space Agency (PhilSa) on Wednesday warned that debris may fall within the designated drop zones near Philippine waters after the launch of a South Korean rocket. The PhilSa earlier confirmed the launch of Korea Space Launch Vehicle-II (KSLV-II) rocket from the Naro Space Center in Goheung, South Jeolla, Republic of Korea, around 11:25 a.m. (Philippine standard time). The rocket reportedly launched a total of 15 satellites to space. The agency identified drop zone (DZ) 1 approximately 387 nautical miles (NM) away from Santa Ana, Cagayan, and 391 NM away from Babuyan Island. READ: PH explores rocket […]...
